You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

What do you mean by “old car makers”? (e.g., makers with the oldest car models in the dataset by `cars_data.Year`, or makers founded earliest—which we *don’t* have in this schema).

If you mean **makers whose cars appear earliest in the dataset**, here are a few useful SQL analyses:

### 1) Oldest year per maker (and how many cars in that maker)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data,
  COUNT(*)     AS cars_count
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC, cars_count DESC;
```

### 2) “Oldest car makers” = makers with cars in the earliest year(s)
```sql
WITH min_year AS (
  SELECT MIN(Year) AS y FROM cars_data
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  cm.Maker,
  cd.Year
FROM min_year
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Year = min_year.y
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
ORDER BY cm.Maker;
```

### 3) Oldest model year per maker + example model(s) in that year
```sql
WITH maker_first_year AS (
  SELECT
    cm.Id AS maker_id,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year
  FROM car_makers cm
  JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
  JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
  JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
  GROUP BY cm.Id
)
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  mfy.first_year,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ml.Model) AS example_models
FROM maker_first_year mfy
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id = mfy.maker_id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId AND cd.Year = mfy.first_year
GROUP BY cm.Maker, mfy.first_year
ORDER BY mfy.first_year, cm.Maker;
```

Tell me which definition you want (oldest-in-dataset vs something else), and whether you want results **by continent/country**, and I can tailor the query.
Focus on makers that produced cars a long time ago.

```sql
-- Makers that produced cars a long time ago (earliest year in the data),
-- plus how many cars they have and their most recent year (to see span).
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS year_span,
  COUNT(*) AS cars_in_data
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year ASC, cars_in_data DESC, cm.Maker;
```

If you want “a long time ago” to mean a cutoff (e.g., makers with any car **≤ 1970**), tell me the year and I’ll adjust the filter.
I want the makers that produced cars a long time ago. Maybe with cars from around 1970 or earlier.

```sql
-- Makers that have at least one car from 1970 or earlier
-- (shows their earliest year and how many cars they have up to 1970)
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  COUNT(*)     AS cars_through_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
WHERE cd.Year <= 1970
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, cars_through_1970 DESC, cm.Maker;
```
Also, include the names of each matching car maker.

```sql
-- Makers with cars from 1970 or earlier, including maker "name" (FullName)
SELECT
  cm.Maker,        -- short name
  cm.FullName,     -- full maker name
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  COUNT(*)     AS cars_through_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
WHERE cd.Year <= 1970
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, cars_through_1970 DESC, cm.Maker;
```
